title: An ALMA Survey of λ Orionis Disks: From Supernovae to Planet Formation
question: Do massive OB stars, in particular a possible supernova ~1 Myr ago, reduce the planet-forming material in the evolved λ Orionis cluster, and why do some massive outlier disks persist in evolved regions?

data.sensitivity: median continuum rms 34 µJy; 3σ dust mass ~0.4 M_earth

what.value: Spectral types, radial velocities of host stars

evidence.quote: References for stellar spectral types (SpT) and radial velocities ( v LSR ): (1) Bayo et al. (2011), (2) Hern´andez et al. (2010)

external_data.citation: Bayo et al. (2011); Hernández et al. (2010); Kounkel et al. (2018) etc.

what.value: Comparison disk dust masses/fluxes for Lupus, σ Ori, Upper Sco, OMC-2

evidence.quote: compares the M dust cumulative distribution for λ Orionis (this work) to that of OMC-2 (van Terwisga et al. 2019a), Lupus (Ansdell et al. 2018)

external_data.citation: van Terwisga et al. 2019a; Ansdell et al. 2018; Ansdell et al. 2017; Barenfeld et al. 2016

what.value: Upper Sco stellar masses for two-sample tests

evidence.quote: Using the M ⋆ values from Table 1 for λ Orionis and those from Barenfeld et al. (2016) for Upper Sco

recipe.method: Spitzer disk census minus debris disks; remove Gaia DR2 background sources and non-member
key_parameters: Gaia DR2 lower distance bound >480 pc

recipe.method: Spectral type and J-band to HR diagram, compare to Baraffe et al. 2015 (Siess et al. 2000 for HD 245185)
split + tclean images; uvmodelfit point source (or elliptical Gaussian for 3 resolved); errors rescaled to reduced chi2=1; stack non-detections
key_parameters: non-detections: position offsets fixed to zero

recipe.method: uvcontsub, spectrum extraction (>3x channel rms), tclean, zero-moment ±3 km/s, curve-of-growth photometry
assumptions: cluster v_LSR 12 km/s if source value unknown

recipe.method: optically thin isothermal relation M_dust ≈ 4.1 × F_1.25mm (M_earth, mJy)
assumptions: T_dust = 20 K, d = 400 pc, optically thin

recipe.goal: Compare dust-mass distributions with other regions
recipe.method: Kaplan-Meier cumulative distributions; T-test and Wilcoxon rank-sum on stellar masses vs Upper Sco
assumptions: Gaia DR2 distances ~150 pc (Lupus, Upper Sco), ~400 pc (σ Ori, OMC-2)

evidence.quote: Only 14 of the 44 sources are detected at ≥ 3 σ significance and only 3 of the detections are marginally resolved.
This results in a median continuum rms of 34 µJy
finding a tentative detection of 0.019 ± 0.006 mJy (3.2 σ) in the stacked image
Only five sources (HD 245185, LO 4155, LO 4187, LO 4407, LO 6866) are detected
the median M dust of the continuum detections in our λ Orionis survey is only ∼ 2 M ⊕ .
median 3 σ upper limit of ∼ 0.4 M ⊕ for the individual non-detections

answer_key.quantity: Stellar mass test p-values vs Upper Sco

evidence.quote: we find p -values of 0.77 and 0.11 for the T-test and Wilcoxon rank-sum test, respectively
